reconcile.note: Adam Clarke reads Paul's anathema in 1 Corinthians 16:22 as a prophetic verdict, not a personal curse, distinguishing it from the cursing Romans 12:14 forbids.

discrepancy.note: Cassels reads Paul's Galatians anathema as showing the same indignant temper Romans 12:14 tells believers to renounce.

quotes.text: The temper of the man is well shown in Paul's indignant letter to the Galatians.…But even though we, or an angel from heaven, should preach unto you any Gospel other than that which we preached to you, let him be accursed. As we have said before, so say I now again: If any man preach any Gospel to you other than that ye received, let him be accursed.
quotes.attr: Walter Richard Cassels (d. 1907), Supernatural Religion, Vol. III (1879), on Galatians 1:8-9.

sides.snippet: Bless those who persecute you; bless, and don't curse.
sides.verseText: Bless those who persecute you; bless, and don't curse.

sides.snippet: If any man doesn't love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed.
sides.verseText: If any man doesn't love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Come, Lord!
